m:rambla: The Boqueria is closed on Sundays. On the Rambla watch out for pickpockets; to eat, move to the side streets.
m:gotic: The streets are free; the tourist visit to the Cathedral costs €16.
m:born: The Born excavations can be seen for free from the covered square. Tourist entry to Santa Maria del Mar is paid: check price and hours on site.
m:barceloneta: On the seafront avoid restaurants with photos of paella on display and waiters calling from the street: the neighbourhood places are in the inner streets.
m:sagrada: From outside it's free. To go in you need a timed ticket (from €26, €36 with the towers) on sagradafamilia.org: same-day tickets are often sold out.
m:passeig: From outside it's all free. Going in costs: Casa Batlló from €29 online, La Pedrera €29 by day (€25 for the sunset visit).
m:sagradains: Basic ticket €26, with the towers €36, timed only, on sagradafamilia.org: buy it before you leave. Shoulders and knees covered.
m:parkguell: Ticket €18 with an entry time, sold from 9:30am to 7:30pm: you enter within 30 minutes of your chosen time and if you leave you can't come back in. Buy it online at parkguell.barcelona. From metro L3 (Vallcarca or Lesseps) it's 15–20 minutes on foot, uphill.
m:gracia: All free. It's the neighbourhood where you eat for less: menú del día at lunch and tapas in the evening in the inner streets.
m:bunkers: Free entry, no booking: open 9am–7:30pm in summer and 9am–5:30pm in winter (changeover dates aren't given: check on site). The last stretch is a steep climb, and at the top there's no water or shade.
m:picasso: Ticket €14 online (€15 at the ticket office), closed on Mondays. From November to April, entry is free on Thursdays from 4 to 7pm.
m:batllo: Blue ticket from €29 online on weekdays and €35 at weekends, if bought at least a week ahead; at the ticket office it costs more. Open every day 8:30am–10:30pm, last entry 9:30pm.
m:santpau: Self-guided visit €18 before 2pm, €17 after. Open every day 9:30am–6:30pm from April to October and 9:30am–5pm from November to March; last entry half an hour before closing.
m:pedrera: Essential ticket €29 (the sunset visit starts from €25). From 6 March to 1 November open 9am–8:30pm, then until February 9am–6:30pm.
m:mnac: The steps and the terrace are free, with outdoor escalators to go up. The MNAC costs €12 and is closed on Mondays.
m:castell: Ticket €12, free on Sundays from 3pm and all day on the first Sunday of the month. Open 10am–8pm from March to October, 10am–6pm from November to February.
vd:colmena: A historic pastry shop between the Gòtic and the Born: Catalan sweets, turrón and honey candies. Buy at the counter and eat as you walk.
vp:colmena: A pastry for a few euros (menu not seen).
vd:conesa: Hot pressed sandwiches a short walk from Plaça Sant Jaume, popular with people who work nearby. Good for breakfast or a quick dinner.
vp:conesa: A sandwich stays under €10 (menu not seen).
vd:elisabets: A neighbourhood bar in the Raval, 5 minutes from Plaça Catalunya: breakfast at the counter and home cooking at lunch. Closed on Sundays.
vd:bodeb: Huge sandwiches filled to order (falafel, chicken, vegetables) on the Mercè's bar street. There's often a queue, but it moves fast.
vp:bodeb: A sandwich stays under €10 (menu not seen).
vd:laplata: A tiny historic bar that serves almost only four things: fried little fish, sausage, tomato salad and anchovies, with the house wine. Standing up or at the barrels.
vp:laplata: With two dishes and a glass you spend around €15 (menu not seen).
vd:hofmann: The Hofmann school's pâtisserie in the Born: famous for its mascarpone-filled croissant. Takeaway only.
vp:hofmann: A pastry for a few euros (menu not seen).
vd:baluard: An artisan bakery in Barceloneta with its wood-fired oven in view: sourdough bread, croissants and Catalan coca.
vd:bombeta: The Barceloneta tapas bar that invented the «bomba», a stuffed potato ball with spicy sauce. Closed on Wednesdays.
vp:bombeta: With two or three tapas you stay under €15 (menu not seen).
vd:montolio: A simple, family-run seafood place in Barceloneta: fried fish, squid and dishes of the day, among the cheapest in the area. There's often a wait.
vd:paixano: The cava bar, standing at the counter: a hot sandwich with sausage or chorizo and a glass of rosé cava. Always full and noisy.
vp:paixano: A sandwich and a couple of glasses for about €8 (from reviews).
vd:canros: A family place in Barceloneta specialising in rice dishes: seafood paella, arròs negre and fideuà, cooked to order. Closed on Mondays.
vp:canros: Arròs negre costs about €17.50 per person (from reviews).
vd:cansole: Open since 1903, it's one of the most renowned rice restaurants in Barceloneta. It costs more but it's a classic. Closed on Mondays.
vd:bodegaros: A neighbourhood bar since 1971: salt cod fritters, artichoke tortilla and the meatball sandwich. Budget range. Closed on Saturdays.
vp:bodegaros: With a sandwich and a tapa you stay under €15 (menu not seen).
vd:tossa: A neighbourhood bar-restaurant five minutes from the Sagrada Família, open all day: breakfast, menú del día and tapas.
vd:bendita: A tapas bar a short walk from the Sagrada Família but popular with locals: patatas bravas, croquettes and tortilla.
vp:bendita: With two or three tapas you spend around €15 (menu not seen).
vd:ciutatcomtal: An always-packed tapas bar on Rambla de Catalunya, halfway between Plaça Catalunya and Passeig de Gràcia: montaditos, croquettes, grilled fish. No bookings.
vp:ciutatcomtal: Mid-range: with three tapas you easily go over €15 (menu not seen).
vd:pastisseria: A high-end pâtisserie in the Eixample, two blocks from Passeig de Gràcia: croissants and individual cakes. Closed on Mondays.
vd:trebol: Freshly fried churros and thick hot chocolate, between the Eixample and Gràcia. From Thursday to Sunday open day and night.
vd:origo: An artisan bakery in Gràcia: sourdough bread, croissants and baked sweets, with a few seats.
vd:casi: A neighbourhood bar in upper Gràcia, on the way to Park Güell: breakfast and home cooking at lunch. Closed on Sundays.
vd:croqroll: Croquettes of every flavour, classic and creative, to eat at a table or take away. Monday to Thursday it only opens in the evening.
vp:croqroll: With a few croquettes and a beer you stay under €15 (menu not seen).
vd:mistral: A neighbourhood bakery opposite the Mercat de Sant Antoni: bread, croissants and coca to take away. Closed on Sundays.
vd:fabrique: A bakery-café at the foot of Montjuïc: sourdough bread, croissants and sandwiches, a few little tables.
vd:tasqueta: A pintxos bar on the pedestrian Carrer de Blai: take them from the counter and pay by counting the sticks.
vp:tasqueta: Pintxos for a few euros each: with five or six you spend around €15 (menu not seen).
cd:vicens: Gaudí's first house, in Gràcia: yellow and green tiled façades, a garden and rooms full of oriental-style decoration.
cd:palauguell: Gaudí's palace a short walk from the Rambla: a large central hall with a dome pierced like a starry sky and a roof of colourful chimneys.
cd:palaumusica: The modernist concert hall, a UNESCO site: stained glass, ceramics and the coloured glass dome. Entry by guided tour.
cd:miro: The Miró museum on Montjuïc hill: paintings, sculptures and a terrace with views over the city.
cd:caixaforum: A former modernist factory turned into an arts centre: temporary exhibitions and a beautiful building to visit.
cd:pobleespanyol: A village built in 1929 with replicas of squares and houses from every region of Spain, craft workshops and bars.
cd:teleferic: The cable car that climbs Montjuïc hill with views of the port and the city, up to the castle.
cx:teleferic: The price is for a return trip. At some times of year the cable car stops for maintenance: check the website.
cd:aquarium: The harbour aquarium: a tunnel under the shark tank and rooms devoted to the Mediterranean.
cd:muhba: The city history museum: under the square you walk among the ruins of Roman Barcino.
cd:gloriestower: Jean Nouvel's bullet-shaped tower: the viewpoint at the top shows the whole city from above.
cn:smaritetti: Santa Maria del Mar, rooftops and crypt
cd:smaritetti: The Born's Gothic church seen from above: you walk on the roofs and go down into the crypt.
cd:tibidabo: Spain's oldest amusement park, at the top of the hill: vintage rides and views down to the sea.
cx:tibidabo: Open only on some days, depending on the season: check the calendar on the official website.
cd:campnou: Barça's stadium with the museum and tours: changing rooms, stands and trophies.
cx:campnou: The stadium is being renovated: access and hours change often, check the club's website.
cd:xocolata: A small museum about the history of chocolate, with sculptures made of chocolate and tastings.
cd:zoo: The zoo in Parc de la Ciutadella: dolphins, monkeys and Mediterranean animals.
cd:amatller: The house next to Casa Batlló, still furnished as it once was: modernist interiors and the chocolate maker Amatller's collection.
cd:macba: The contemporary art museum in the Raval: a large white building by Richard Meier and a square where people skateboard.
cd:maritim: Inside the old medieval shipyards, a gallery with ships, maps and a replica of the galley from Lepanto.
cd:pedralbes: A Gothic monastery with a three-storey cloister, in a quiet neighbourhood above the city.
